final_answer:
CHARTER-OFFERING DEVIATION REPORT: ATHERTON BIOMEDICAL, INC. IPO

Documents: (C) Fourth A&R Charter (6/22/2023); (UA) Underwriting Agreement (1/6/2025); (P) Preliminary Prospectus (1/3/2025). Statutory points come from my own knowledge. Egress to eCFR and the Delaware Code was blocked, so they are NOT independently verified.

I. BOTTOM LINE
The UA (Sec. 6(j)) and the prospectus describe a post-IPO charter (the "IPO Charter") that the Fourth A&R Charter does not contain and in several respects contradicts. UA Exhibit A is circular: it "attaches" the Fourth A&R Charter as the form of IPO Charter, yet that form violates nearly every Sec. 6(j) requirement. Separately, the three documents disagree on the over-allotment size and on share counts, and the prospectus financial tables do not tie. Priority items are marked CRITICAL, HIGH or MEDIUM.

II. CHARTER vs. UA SEC. 6(j) (closing condition) vs. PROSPECTUS

1. Authorized common (HIGH). C 4.1: 100,000,000. UA 6(j)(i) and P (Capitalization; Description of Capital Stock): 200,000,000. UA 3(b) correctly represents 100,000,000 as of signing. Fix: the IPO Charter must increase the authorization, which needs a Sec. 242 vote.

2. Series A/B/C elimination (HIGH). UA 6(j)(ii) speaks of eliminating "certificates of designation." The series are not set out in certificates of designation. They are hard-wired into C 4.4-4.6 and 4.7. The IPO Charter must delete those sections and Sec. 5.5 (preferred director seats). P says the series "designations will be eliminated."
Timing and mechanics: C 4.4(d)/4.5(d)/4.6(d) convert automatically on the "closing" of a Qualified IPO (at least $50M gross proceeds to the Company and at least $10.00 per share). P says conversion occurs "immediately prior" to completion. UA 6(j) allows the charter to be filed "at or prior to" closing. UA 4(e) requires the Selling Stockholders' preferred to have converted before closing so they can deliver common. The charter has no conditional-conversion mechanic.
Filing the IPO Charter before closing needs the separate class and protective-provision consents (A 4.4(f)(i)/(g)(i): majority; B 4.5(f)/(g): majority; C 4.6(f)/(g): 60%; also Sec. 242(b)(2) class votes). Filing after closing is incompatible with UA 6(j). Action: confirm the consent and conversion sequence. Qualified IPO thresholds are met at $18-$20 but not below $10.

3. Classified board (CRITICAL). C 5.3: all directors elected annually. UA 6(j)(iii) and P: three staggered classes. The charter has no classes. UA says the IPO Charter sets the initial class assignments, but P does not disclose which of the seven directors (Nagarajan, Marchetti, Durand-Phelps, Okonkwo, Rajagopal, Belasco, Fong) sits in which class.

5. Director removal (HIGH). C is silent. The Delaware default is removal with or without cause (DGCL 141(k)), unless the board is classified, in which case removal is for cause only. UA 6(j)(iv) and P: for cause only, by 66 2/3%. The 66 2/3% vote must be written into the charter. C 5.4 (vacancies filled by the board) is consistent with P, but P never mentions vacancies.

6. Written consent (CRITICAL). C 6.3 expressly permits action by written consent. UA 6(j)(vi) and P prohibit it from closing. This is a DGCL 228 charter-level change, so a bylaw is not enough.

7. Special meetings (HIGH, omission). C 6.2 lets holders of 25% of the voting power compel a special meeting. UA and P are silent. If the IPO Charter is built from the Exhibit A form, this right survives and contradicts P's description of anti-takeover protections. P (Description of Capital Stock) also omits who may call special meetings.

8. Cumulative voting (MEDIUM). C is silent. Cumulative voting is not available unless the charter grants it (DGCL 214), so the default is no cumulative voting. UA 6(j)(v) and P require an express denial.

9. Exclusive forum (HIGH). Three versions conflict:
- C 8.1: Chancery, then Superior Court, then D. Del. Covers fiduciary claims against directors, officers, employees "or agents." No federal-securities forum.
- UA 6(j)(vii)(A): Chancery, then "another state court" in Delaware, then D. Del. Covers directors, officers, or employees (no "agents"). Adds a Securities Act federal forum.
- P: Chancery, then federal D. Del. only (omits the state-court tier). Covers directors, officers, or "other employees." Adds the federal forum and notes that the Exchange Act is excluded.
Action: pick one text and conform all three documents. The federal forum provision is facially valid under Salzberg v. Sciabacucchi, 227 A.3d 102 (Del. 2020), which I recall but did not re-verify.

10. Supermajority amendment (HIGH). C Art. X: a majority vote suffices to amend. UA 6(j)(viii) and P: 66 2/3% to amend the classified board, removal, written-consent and forum provisions. A gap shared by UA and P: neither requires a supermajority to amend the supermajority provision itself or the bylaws, and P says "all other provisions" need only a majority.

11. DGCL Sec. 203 (CRITICAL). C Art. IX opts out expressly. UA 6(j)(ix) requires the IPO Charter to contain no opt-out. P says Sec. 203 will apply. Action: delete Art. IX. Diligence whether Redhill/Solstice become "interested stockholders."

12. Anti-dilution and preferential rights (HIGH). C 4.4(e)/4.5(e): broad-based weighted average. C 4.6(e): Series C full ratchet. C 4.6(b): Series C participation capped at 3x. C 4.6(h): redemption at 60% election after year five. C 4.6(g)(v): consent right over debt above $10M. UA 6(j)(x) requires all of these to be eliminated, and it specifically names the Series C full-ratchet and participation rights. P is silent on the Series C ratchet, the 3x participation, the redemption right and the debt consent right. This is a disclosure gap: the pre-IPO terms are not described, and there is no "Description of Preferred Stock" disclosing the rights being terminated.

13. Preferred authorized-share overshoot (CRITICAL). C 4.1 authorizes only 25,000,000 preferred shares. C 4.4-4.6 designate 8,200,000 + 11,650,000 + 6,800,000 = 26,650,000 shares, which is 1,650,000 more than authorized. UA 3(b) and 6(j) and P all treat 26,650,000 preferred shares as duly authorized, validly issued and convertible. Potential invalid or defective stock (DGCL 204/205 ratification may be needed). This affects the UA 3(b) "duly authorized and validly issued" representation, the Hargrove Whitfield opinion (UA 6(e)) and the conversion count.

14. Series C debt consent versus disclosed debt (HIGH). C 4.6(g)(v) requires 60% Series C consent for indebtedness above $10,000,000, excluding trade payables and equipment financing. P discloses total debt of $41.3M. No UA representation covers compliance with the charter or the consent. Obtain the consent or a waiver and add a representation.

15. Drafting (MEDIUM). C 4.4(d) is missing its "(i)" label; C 7.1-7.2 (exculpation/indemnification) are not described in P.

III. UA vs. PROSPECTUS

16. Over-allotment option (CRITICAL). UA Sec. 1 and 2(b): 1,725,000 shares, 15% of firm shares. P cover, Offering summary, Use of Proceeds, Capitalization fn 4, Underwriting: 1,500,000 shares. Consequence for full exercise at $19.00:
- Shares sold in total: 13,225,000.
- Public offering price, total: $251,275,000 (P shows $247,000,000).
- Underwriting discount: $16,332,875 (P shows $16,055,000).
- Proceeds to the Company: $181,647,125 (P shows $177,650,000).
- Use of Proceeds and Capitalization leave the over-allotment figures blank (the $[●] placeholders).

17. Lock-up (HIGH).
- Measuring date: UA Sec. 1, 5(i) and 6(i): 180 days after the final Prospectus. UA Exh. C (the form every holder signs): 180 days after the date of the Underwriting Agreement (1/6/2025), which expires about eight days early relative to the pricing date. P: "from the date of this prospectus."
- Who is bound: UA 6(i): directors, officers, and 1% holders. P summary: "we, directors and executive officers, and the selling stockholders." P Description/Underwriting: "holders of substantially all" common and convertibles. These are three different populations.
- Exceptions: Exh. C includes domestic-relations orders, capped-free tax withholding, registration-demand restrictions and exercise of options. P adds exceptions for will and intestate succession and nominee or custodian transfers. P treats the tax-withholding exception as capped by a number "[●]." Exh. C has no cap. P describes 10b5-1 plans "established prior to the offering" while Exh. C permits establishment of a plan with no sales.
- Company lock-up: UA 5(i) carve-outs (shares issued in the offering, options exercised, plan grants conditioned on recipients' lock-ups) are not described in P. P's company lock-up adds "lend," which UA 5(i) lacks.

18. Equity plan (HIGH). UA 5(h) covenants an evergreen of 4% of shares outstanding on the preceding December 31 and gives no board discretion. P: 4% of shares outstanding on "January 1" (Equity Incentive Plan) or "the last day of the immediately preceding fiscal year" (Capitalization fn 3), "unless our board determines a lesser number." P says 3,200,000 options and RSUs sit "under prior plans or awards assumed or rolled into" the 2024 plan, yet P treats the 5,080,000 reserve as additional. UA 1 says the 2024 plan was stockholder-approved; P is silent.

19. Underwriter default and expenses (HIGH). P (Underwriting): says the UA provides that if an underwriter defaults, the others' commitments may increase or the UA may terminate. The UA contains no default provision. P says the Company will reimburse "certain" underwriter expenses with no limit. UA Sec. 9 reimburses only if the offering fails through the Company's breach, capped at $300,000, and otherwise makes the Underwriters pay their own counsel. P gives no FINRA compensation disclosure on this.

21. Settlement (MEDIUM). UA Sec. 1 and 2(c): Closing T+3 (January 17 after a January 14 pricing). The standard cycle since May 28, 2024 is T+1 under Exchange Act Rule 15c6-1 (my recollection, not re-verified). Rule 15c6-1(c) allows T+2 for certain firm-commitment offerings priced after 4:30 p.m. ET. T+3 would require an express agreement and is out of line with the rule. P is silent on the closing date.

22. Conflicts and parties (MEDIUM). Diane Kowalski signs the charter, is the Company notice party and Exh. D attorney-in-fact for the Selling Stockholders. Gregory Okonkwo (Redhill) and Sunita Rajagopal (Solstice) sign for Selling Stockholders and are directors. P does not identify the Selling Stockholders anywhere (the cover says they are "identified in this prospectus") and contains no principal/selling stockholders table (Item 507 of Regulation S-K).

IV. SHARE COUNT AND FINANCIAL TIE-OUT

24. Share count (CRITICAL). UA 3(b) and P state 42,350,000 shares outstanding "as converted." Components: 12,500,000 founder shares + 26,650,000 preferred-as-converted + 3,200,000 options and RSUs. Options and RSUs are not outstanding shares. P then separately "excludes" the same 3,200,000 options. P's actual common of 15,700,000 (par $15,700) = 12.5M + 3.2M. Correct outstanding is 39,150,000 pre-offering and 47,650,000 post-offering (not 50,850,000). It affects P's 39,350,000 "restricted" shares, the 83.3% / 16.7% ownership split, per-share NTBV and "10% of outstanding" plan sizing (5,080,000 / 47,650,000 = 10.66%).

25. Preferred carrying values (MEDIUM). P: A $32.8M, B $58.25M, C $40.8M ($131.85M). C issue prices imply $12.3M, $49.51M, $59.5M ($121.31M); reconcile.

26. Proceeds and equity (HIGH). The $151,002,500 net proceeds are stated "after deducting estimated offering expenses" (P, Use of Proceeds) but equal gross proceeds less the discount only (8,500,000 x $17.765). UA 2(a) correctly says "before other offering expenses." Pro forma as adjusted cash ($215,702,500) therefore ignores expenses. APIC rises $150,951,650 versus $150,994,000 implied (8,500,000 x $17.765 less $8,500 par): a $42,350 difference.

27. NTBV versus equity (HIGH). P Dilution: pro forma NTBV $148.2M ($3.50) and $299.2M ($5.88) exceed pro forma equity in Capitalization ($109.4M and $260.4M). NTBV cannot exceed stockholders' equity. "Total consideration" from existing stockholders ($148,225,000) is NTBV x shares, not consideration paid. P's summary financial data is described as derived from audited statements but includes unaudited TTM and 9/30/2024 data. Expert section covers 12/31/2023 and 2022 balance sheets and three-year results.

VI. RECOMMENDED ACTIONS
1) Draft and attach a real IPO Charter as UA Exhibit A. Include items 1-12 and conform the forum text.
2) Cure the 1,650,000 excess preferred shares before closing (DGCL 204/205 ratification) and obtain the Series C debt-consent waiver.
3) Fix the sequencing of consents, conversion and charter filing; add a conditional-conversion mechanism.
4) Conform the over-allotment size (1,725,000 or 1,500,000) throughout.
5) Fix share counts, NTBV and offering-expense math, and correct the lock-up and settlement mechanics.
6) Complete the Selling Stockholder, related-party and Series C disclosure; correct the Underwriting section.
